literal: The emperor was angry and stripped his title.
idiomatic: The emperor was furious and stripped his title.

literal: His son Yan, styled Qihuti, had considerable force of character.
idiomatic: His son Yan, styled Qihuti, had real backbone.

literal: He inherited Duke of Henan; by precedent the title was reduced and he was re-enfeoffed Marquis of Ruyang.
idiomatic: He inherited Duke of Henan; by rule it was lowered to Marquis of Ruyang.

literal: He held Great General of Huaishuo Garrison and Minister of the Imperial Stud.
idiomatic: He was Great General of Huaishuo Garrison and Minister of the Imperial Stud.

literal: Sent to soothe Xiurong, he was killed by herdsmen.
idiomatic: Sent to pacify Xiurong, he was killed by herdsmen.

literal: Lu Luoba was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Lu Luoba was a man of Dai.

literal: Great-grandfather Kehou in Zhaocheng's time led five thousand households to submit to Wei.
idiomatic: Great-grandfather Kehou in Zhaocheng's time led five thousand households to Wei.

literal: His father Pizhi in Taiwu's time was western tribal chief and enfeoffed Duke of Xingyang.
idiomatic: His father Pizhi under Taiwu was western tribal chief, Duke of Xingyang.

literal: Luoba was known for stalwart courage.
idiomatic: Luoba was known for courage.

literal: At the end of Wencheng he was Chief Commander of Pingyuan Garrison.
idiomatic: At Wencheng's end he was Chief Commander of Pingyuan Garrison.

literal: Following Wei Yuan attacking Song general Zhang Yong, he routed him greatly and was granted Marquis of Chengwu.
idiomatic: With Wei Yuan against Song's Zhang Yong he won a great rout and was made Marquis of Chengwu.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Eldest son Wenzu — Xianwen, because he was a meritorious minister's son, made him supplemental Dragon Herds Office Memorial Drafter and Central Attendant.
idiomatic: Eldest son Wenzu — Xianwen, as a hero's son, made him supplemental Memorial Drafter in the Dragon Herds Office and Central Attendant.

literal: Because herds did not thrive he was demoted to Wuchuan Garrison.
idiomatic: When herds failed to thrive he was sent to Wuchuan Garrison.

literal: Later Wenzu translated and annotated the imperial pronouncements in the old tongue; his wording was fluent and clear, and he was Memorial Drafter in the Outer Office.
idiomatic: Later Wenzu translated the imperial edicts in the old tongue with fluent clarity and became Outer Office Memorial Drafter.

literal: Later he was executed for an offense.
idiomatic: Later he was executed for an offense.

literal: Xue Biaozi was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Xue Biaozi was a man of Dai.

literal: Grandfather Datou from Yao Chang's time led the tribe to submit to Wei.
idiomatic: Grandfather Datou in Yao Chang's time led the tribe to Wei.

literal: Daowu granted Marquis of Liaocheng and treated him with honored-guest rites, giving Lady Zheng in marriage.
idiomatic: Daowu made him Marquis of Liaocheng, treated him as honored guest, and gave him Lady Zheng.

literal: He died; posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou, posthumous title Mournful.
idiomatic: At death posthumously Governor of Jizhou, styled Mournful.

literal: His father Yeying was Governor of Bing and Tai, enfeoffed Duke of Hedong, with a sounding reputation.
idiomatic: His father Yeying was Governor of Bing and Tai, Duke of Hedong, well spoken of.

literal: He died; posthumous title Simple.
idiomatic: He died, styled Simple.

literal: Biaozi was imposing in appearance, clear in judgment, with his father's manner.
idiomatic: Biaozi was imposing, clear-judging, his father's son.

literal: He was Inner Conduct Director, overseeing memorial affairs of the various offices.
idiomatic: He was Inner Conduct Director, overseeing the offices' memorials.

literal: Upright in office, within and without they feared him.
idiomatic: Upright in office — all feared him.

literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, he went out as Garrison Commander of Fangtou.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming ruled, he went out as Fangtou Garrison Commander.

literal: By nature stern and simple, he was envied by near ministers;
idiomatic: Stern and plain by nature, near ministers envied him;

literal: for a small fault he was demoted to garrison gate guard.
idiomatic: for a small fault he was reduced to garrison gate guard.

literal: When Xianwen toured south and halted at Shanyang, Biaozi appealed on the road and was again appointed Fangtou Garrison Commander.
idiomatic: When Xianwen went south and stopped at Shanyang, Biaozi appealed on the road and was again Fangtou commander.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted Opening Office and Governor of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: He rose to Opening Office and Governor of Xuzhou.

literal: In the province he had many benevolent policies; the people found him convenient.
idiomatic: In the province he ruled with mercy; the people were at ease.

literal: Pei commandery Administrator Shao An and Xiapi Administrator Zhang Pan were both corrupt; Biaozi prosecuted them by law.
idiomatic: Pei Administrator Shao An and Xiapi Administrator Zhang Pan were corrupt; Biaozi tried them by law.

literal: An and the rest sent younger brothers to memorialize, falsely accusing Biaozi of secretly communicating with southern bandits.
idiomatic: They sent younger kin to accuse Biaozi of secretly aiding southern bandits.

literal: Xiaowen said: "This is false."
idiomatic: Xiaowen said, "This is nonsense."

literal: Investigation proved it empty.
idiomatic: Investigation proved it empty.

literal: He died; posthumous title Literary.
idiomatic: He died, styled Literary.

literal: His son Zhu.
idiomatic: His son Zhu.

literal: Zhu, styled Tanzhen, was striking in form and appearance.
idiomatic: Zhu, styled Tanzhen, was striking to look upon.

literal: In youth for capability he was made Director of Guests.
idiomatic: Young, capable, he was made Director of Guests.

literal: Whenever summoned to audience his bearing was very fine.
idiomatic: Each audience found his bearing fine.

literal: Xuanwu said to him: "Your manner is stern and whole, your appearance outstanding — you will rise later; how do you see your office?"
idiomatic: Xuanwu said, "Your bearing is whole, your looks outstanding — you will rise; how do you see your post?"

literal: Zhu answered: "In ancestral temple rites I dare not fail in reverence;
idiomatic: Zhu answered, "In ancestral rites I dare not fail in reverence;

literal: in court affairs I dare not fail in loyalty.
idiomatic: in court affairs I dare not fail in loyalty.

literal: Beyond this, it is not for a mediocre minister to reach."
idiomatic: Beyond that, a mediocre minister cannot reach."

literal: In Zhengguang he acted as Magistrate of Luoyang; within his district all was orderly.
idiomatic: In Zhengguang he acted Luoyang Magistrate; the district was orderly.

literal: Because of long drought, capital prisoners were all gathered at the capital pavilion to examine delayed wrongs.
idiomatic: In long drought, capital prisoners were gathered at the capital pavilion to clear delayed wrongs.

literal: Luoyang's prison held only three men.
idiomatic: Luoyang's prison held only three men.

literal: Xiaoming commended this and granted a hundred bolts of silk.
idiomatic: Xiaoming praised this and gave a hundred bolts of silk.

literal: Zhu had earlier attached to Yuan Cha; when Cha was deposed he was anxious and fearful — from this governance and teaching slackened, and he was removed from office.
idiomatic: Zhu had clung to Yuan Cha; when Cha fell he was afraid — rule slackened and he was dismissed.

literal: Li Shengui had favor with Empress Dowager Ling; Zhu again served him.
idiomatic: Li Shengui had Ling Empress Dowager's favor; Zhu served him again.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: He rose to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

literal: Earlier, Minister of Personnel Cui Liang had memorialized establishing the seniority-stop rule, not sorting talent, asking only seniority and old service.
idiomatic: Earlier Minister Cui Liang had proposed the seniority-stop rule — no sorting by talent, only years and old service.

literal: Zhu then submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that though brocade is light, one does not entrust learning to cut with it;
idiomatic: Zhu memorialized: "I hear that though brocade is light, one does not use it to learn cutting;

literal: though ritual vessels are heavy, one cannot entrust them to weak strength.
idiomatic: though ritual vessels are heavy, one does not set them on weak shoulders.

literal: If the selection office takes only years of service and does not sort worthy from unworthy, it makes righteousness equal to flying geese in line.
idiomatic: If selection takes only seniority, not worth, it makes merit a line of geese.

literal: Next, strung like fish on a skewer, checking registers and calling names — one clerk suffices.
idiomatic: Strung like fish on a skewer, one clerk calling names from the register suffices.

literal: What then is the meaning of weighing and balancing?"
idiomatic: Why then keep a Ministry of Personnel?"

literal: Now the people's lives hang on prefects and magistrates.
idiomatic: Now the people's lives hang on prefects and magistrates.

literal: If they get the right men, there is ground for revival;
idiomatic: If the right men are found, the land can breathe again;

literal: if the wrong men are set in office, the harm goes deeper.
idiomatic: if the wrong men are set, harm runs deeper.

literal: Your servant asks that commandery and county posts — the Ministry first choose talent throughout, all who have mastered classics and histories and understand governing — to meet selection.
idiomatic: Let commandery and county posts be filled first from talent who know classics, histories, and rule.

literal: Not bound by distance of entry, amount of years or merit — among accumulated service, any with talent fit to shepherd people should stand within the first-use limit.
idiomatic: Do not bind by years alone; among the long-serving, any fit to govern should be used first.

literal: The rest unfit — now in their prime you borrow their strength; how can you cast them off in old age?"
idiomatic: The rest, unfit but still strong — how cast them off when old?"

literal: Adjutants, aides, assistants, and commandants are somewhat farther from the people; small right and wrong are not great loss — they should be filled in order to repay their labor."
idiomatic: Deputies and aides are farther from the people; small errors matter less — fill them in order to repay labor."

literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply.
idiomatic: The memorial went in; no reply.

literal: Later on being summoned to audience he again stated: "Now the four quarters are newly settled; the task is to nurture the people.
idiomatic: Later at audience he said again, "The realm is newly settled; the task is to nurture the people.

literal: Your servant asks to follow Han precedent and newly establish four categories, ordering the Three Dukes and noble ministers each to recommend men of the time to supplement commanderies and counties.
idiomatic: I ask to follow Han and renew the four categories, letting Three Dukes and nobles each recommend talent for commanderies and counties.

literal: Clearly set rules to guard against factions.
idiomatic: Set clear rules against factions.

literal: Perhaps then the people in ashes and charcoal may have ground to look up."
idiomatic: Then perhaps those in ashes may have something to look up to."

literal: An edict was sent down to the Three Dukes and ministers for discussion; the matter also lay dormant.
idiomatic: An edict went to the Three Dukes for discussion; the matter also died.

literal: Yuan Tianmu campaigned against Xing Guo and made Zhu Mobile-Office Minister.
idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu campaigned against Xing Guo and made Zhu Mobile-Office Minister.

literal: The army halted at Dongjun; then Yuan Hao had already seized Zancheng, and Xing Guo also pressed Lixia; Tianmu debated which to strike first.
idiomatic: The army stopped at Dongjun; Yuan Hao held Zancheng, Xing Guo pressed Lixia; Tianmu debated priority.

literal: Discussants all said Guo was strong and the border should be taken first.
idiomatic: All said Guo was strong and the border should come first.

literal: Only Zhu held that Guo was a mob without a name — though strong, still a bandit.
idiomatic: Only Zhu said Guo was a nameless mob — strong, but still bandits.

literal: Yuan Hao was the imperial clan's close kin, coming in the name of righteous rising.
idiomatic: Yuan Hao was imperial kin, coming under the banner of righteous rising.

literal: Since the battle at Heyin the people's hearts were shocked and resentful; now there is a chance — easy to stir feeling.
idiomatic: Since Heyin hearts were shocked; now a chance stirs them easily.

literal: Wait until Hao's affair is settled, then turn the army.
idiomatic: Settle Hao first, then turn the army.

literal: Tianmu followed the crowd's wish and first attacked Guo.
idiomatic: Tianmu followed the crowd and struck Guo first.

literal: Guo surrendered; the army returned to Dingtao; Tianmu left Zhu to act for Western Yanzhou.
idiomatic: Guo surrendered; returning to Dingtao, Tianmu left Zhu acting for Western Yanzhou.

literal: Soon he was trapped by Yuan Hao.
idiomatic: Soon he was trapped by Yuan Hao.

literal: Hao seized Zhu and kept him with him.
idiomatic: Hao seized Zhu and kept him at his side.

literal: Erzhu Rong broke Hao; Tianmu said to Zhu: "Had we not used your words, it would have come to this!"
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong broke Hao; Tianmu told Zhu, "Had we heeded you, we would not be here!"

literal: At the start of Tianping he was appointed Minister of the Seven Arms.
idiomatic: At Tianping's start he was Minister of the Seven Arms.

literal: Qi Shenwu drew him as Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Office; military and state affairs he knew much of.
idiomatic: Qi Shenwu made him Chief Clerk; he knew much of army and state.

literal: Zhu also pushed sincerity to the limit, repeatedly offering loyal remonstrance.
idiomatic: Zhu too gave full sincerity, offering loyal remonstrance again and again.

literal: Shenwu made a great western campaign and was about to cross the Pu ford.
idiomatic: Shenwu marched west in force and was about to cross the Pu ford.

literal: Zhu remonstrated: "Western bandits have suffered famine for years; therefore they risk death to enter Shaanzhou.
idiomatic: Zhu urged: "Western foes have starved for years; they risk death to enter Shaanzhou.

literal: Only place troops on every road and do not meet them in field battle.
idiomatic: Only post troops on every road; do not fight in the open.

literal: By next year's wheat harvest people should starve to death; Bao Ju and Hei Da will naturally submit.
idiomatic: By next harvest they will starve; Bao Ju and Hei Da will submit of themselves.

literal: I beg you not to cross the river."
idiomatic: I beg you not to cross the river."

literal: Hou Jing also said: "Now the army raised is at its utmost; ten thousand in one will not succeed — hard to gather in at the end.
idiomatic: Hou Jing also said, "This army is raised to the limit; one chance in ten thousand — hard to pull back.

literal: Better divide into two armies and advance in succession; if the first wins, the second joins force;
idiomatic: Better split into two armies in succession; if the first wins, the second adds force;

literal: if the first loses, the second takes it up."
idiomatic: if the first loses, the second takes it up."

literal: Shenwu accepted neither and thus had the defeat at Shayuan.
idiomatic: Shenwu took neither counsel and met defeat at Shayuan.

literal: Later Fanyang Lu Zhongli rebelled; Zhu with the various armies pacified him.
idiomatic: Later Lu Zhongli of Fanyang rebelled; Zhu with other armies pacified him.

literal: He was transferred Governor of Yinzhou.
idiomatic: He was transferred Governor of Yinzhou.

literal: His governance was harsh; officials and people suffered.
idiomatic: He ruled harshly; officials and people suffered.

literal: Later he held in succession the two ministries of Revenue and Palace.
idiomatic: Later he held the ministries of Revenue and Palace in turn.

literal: In the first year of Tianbao he died while Acting Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In Tianbao year one he died as Acting Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At the end he charged his sons to bury him in timely dress.
idiomatic: Dying, he ordered his sons to bury him in plain timely dress.
